skill.name: design-an-interface
skill.description: Generate multiple radically different interface designs for a module using parallel sub-agents. Use when user wants to design an API, explore interface options, compare module shapes, or mentions "design it twice".
skill.summary: Generate and compare contrasting software interface designs before implementation.
skill.author: mattpocock

security_audit.summary: The only static finding points to a Markdown fenced prompt template in SKILL.md, not executable Ruby or shell code. No semantic prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or unsafe operational behavior was found.

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md lines 28-46 contain a Markdown code fence for a sub-agent prompt template. It does not execute commands or instruct the agent to run shell code.

content.value_statement: First API drafts often expose the wrong abstractions. This skill generates contrasting module interface designs and compares trade-offs before implementation.
actual_capabilities: Guides requirements gathering before interface design starts.
Prompts multiple sub-agents to create radically different designs.
Structures each design around signatures, usage, hidden complexity, and trade-offs.
Compares options using simplicity, depth, flexibility, efficiency, and misuse risk.
Helps synthesize a final direction from multiple interface proposals.
limitations: It does not implement the selected interface.
It depends on clear module requirements from the user.
It works best for software module interfaces, not visual user interfaces.
It cannot verify runtime performance without implementation details.

use_cases.title: Plan a New API
use_cases.description: Explore several shapes for a new module before committing to one public contract.

use_cases.title: Refine Internal Boundaries
use_cases.description: Compare interface options for a service, adapter, or domain module during architecture planning.

use_cases.title: Review Design Alternatives
use_cases.description: Use explicit trade-offs to discuss API choices before code review starts.

prompt_templates.title: Start Simple
prompt_templates.prompt: Design three interface options for my module. Ask clarifying questions first if requirements are missing.

prompt_templates.title: Compare API Shapes
prompt_templates.prompt: Design radically different interfaces for this module, then compare simplicity, flexibility, depth, and misuse risk.
prompt_templates.scenario: Choosing between several possible API directions

prompt_templates.title: Stress Constraints
prompt_templates.prompt: Design interfaces for this module under separate constraints: minimal methods, maximum flexibility, common-case speed, and future extensibility.
prompt_templates.scenario: Evaluating a module with competing design pressures

prompt_templates.title: Synthesize a Final Direction
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate four interface designs, critique each one, and recommend a final hybrid design with clear rejected alternatives.

output_examples.input: A cache module needs get, set, expire, and invalidation behavior.
output_examples.output: The skill returns several interface styles, usage examples, hidden implementation details, and a prose comparison of trade-offs.

output_examples.input: A payment adapter must support multiple providers without leaking provider details.
output: A workflow-oriented interface with trade-off notes.

output_examples.input: A validation library needs a public API for forms and backend services.
output_examples.output: The skill contrasts fluent, schema-based, and function-first designs, then recommends a direction based on caller needs.

best_practices: Provide caller types, key operations, constraints, and hidden implementation details.
Ask for designs that optimize for different goals.
Compare designs before selecting or combining ideas.
anti_patterns: Do not use it to generate implementation code.
Do not accept similar designs without requesting stronger contrast.
Do not skip requirements gathering for complex modules.

faq.question: Is this for visual interface design?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on software module interfaces, APIs, and caller-facing contracts.

faq.question: Does it write production code?
faq.answer: No. It helps choose the interface shape before implementation starts.

faq.question: Why does it generate multiple designs?
faq.answer: Multiple designs expose trade-offs that a single first draft can hide.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: What input should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the module purpose, callers, key operations, constraints, and details that should stay internal.

faq.question: What should I do after using it?
faq.answer: Select a design, combine useful ideas, then implement and test the chosen interface.
